note: base64url check-order negative vectors v0 (design draft v0.4.2 §4.6: canonicality before length). Generated with the frozen implementation; each case gives the raw input string, the expected byte length (expected_length), the name of the length category (length_category), the layer (layer), the check that fires first (fires: charset | mod4_length | trailing_bits | byte_length; null for valid cases) and the expected result (expect: valid or an error category). A string that is both non-canonical AND of the wrong length must report non_canonical_base64url, never a length error.
order: charset (b64url alphabet, no padding) -> mod-4 decodable length (len % 4 != 1) -> re-encode byte-identical (zero trailing bits) -> decoded byte length == expected

cases.name: sig_valid_control
cases.why: canonical 86-char encoding of 64 bytes (bytes(range(64))); decodes and re-encodes byte-identical

cases.name: trailing_bits_wrong_length_canonicity_first
cases.why: round-1 probe: decodes to 1 byte with 4 nonzero trailing bits AND the wrong length; canonicality must fire first, never signature_length

cases.name: mod4_undecodable_wrong_length_canonicity_first
cases.why: round-1 probe: length % 4 == 1 can never decode; undecodable = non-canonical, not a length error

cases.name: trailing_bits_correct_length
cases.why: length is the canonical 86, but the final sextet leaves 4 nonzero trailing bits

cases.name: charset_padding
cases.why: padding '=' is outside the canonical alphabet

cases.name: charset_foreign_alphabet
cases.why: '+' and '/' are standard-base64 characters; foreign alphabet AND wrong length — charset fires first

cases.name: canonical_but_wrong_length_sig
cases.why: a perfectly canonical decodable string (32 bytes) whose byte count != expected: pure length error

cases.name: canonical_8char_expected_5
cases.why: canonical 6-byte string, 5 requested: pure length error (mirrors the round-1 unit case)

cases.name: both_noncanonical_and_wrong_length_sig_path
cases.why: nonzero trailing bits (2) AND 32 != 64 bytes: the canonicality check wins on the signature path

cases.name: key_valid_control
cases.why: canonical 43-char encoding of 32 bytes; the public-key path shares decode_strict

cases.name: key_trailing_bits_wrong_length
cases.why: same order on the key path: canonicality before public_key_length

cases.name: key_trailing_bits_correct_length
cases.why: canonical 43-char length, but the final sextet leaves 2 nonzero trailing bits

cases.name: key_canonical_but_wrong_length
cases.why: canonical 64-byte string where 32 bytes are expected: pure length error on the key path
